chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Al-Fadl ibn Ismail al-Hashimi, from his father, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what I faced from my family regarding their taking the religion lightly. He said: 'O Ismail, do not find it strange that from your family, for indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made for every family a proof by which He argues against its members on the Day of Resurrection. It will be said to them: 'Did you not see so-and-so among you? Did you not see his guidance among you? Did you not see his prayer among you? Did you not see his religion? Why did you not follow him?' So he will become a proof against them on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.اسْتِخْفَاف: Taking something lightly,轻视, or showing negligence/disregard
key_terms.اقْتَدَى: To follow or emulate as a role model
key_terms.حُجَّة: Proof or evidence used by God to argue against or for individuals on the Day of Resurrection

ai.seo_question: How does a righteous family member serve as a proof against their relatives on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reassures Isma'il ibn Ja'far that the neglect of religious duties by one's own family is a common trial, as Allah designates a pious 'hujjah' (proof) within every lineage to serve as a clear standard of guidance. On the Day of Judgment, this individual’s exemplary prayer, conduct, and faith will be cited as evidence against their relatives for their failure to emulate the spiritual excellence present among them. This highlights the Shia concept of familial accountability, where proximity to righteousness increases one's responsibility to follow it.
